CREAMERY

At our certified Organic and Biodynamic® Creamery, we craft yogurt, buttermilk and quark, and bottle raw and pasteurized milk from the rich, grass-fed milk of our mixed-breed dairy herd—raised with care, kept with their calves, and tended to in harmony with regenerative principles that nourish the land, animals, and people.

THE COWS
Learn More About Our Beloved Dairy Herd
Our Unique, Dual-Purpose Herd

Most of the milk for our Organic and Biodynamic® creamery comes from our mixed-breed cows — primarily Brown Swiss, with some Jersey, Guernsey, Devon, Normande, and Angus. Over time, they’ve become a farm-specific breed, selected for thriving on homegrown forages, strong legs for pasture walks, and gentle dispositions — a must with so many farm visitors. The Brown Swiss, Jersey, and Guernsey genetics contribute higher fat and protein levels, ideal for our cheeses, yogurts, and rich cream lines. The addition of Normande (2017) and Angus (2023) has improved meat quality. Our goal: dual-purpose cows that excel on 100% pasture, producing exceptional milk and meat.

CREAMERY PRODUCTS

Crafted with care from our own grass-fed cows Hawthorne Valley’s creamery products reflect our commitment to animal welfare, soil health, and the delicious potential of regenerative dairy.

Yogurt

Our cup-set, European-style yogurt is crafted in small batches on the farm using fresh, whole milk from our own grass-fed cows and a few trusted local dairies. We keep it pure—no thickeners, stabilizers, or fillers—just rich, unhomogenized milk that forms a naturally creamy layer on top.

Available in four delicious flavors—Plain (Demeter Certified Biodynamic®), Maple, Honey, and Coffee (all USDA Organic)—our yogurt is also proudly Real Organic Project certified. Light, refreshing, and deeply satisfying, it’s often described as tasting just like homemade. We consider that the highest praise.

Raw + Pasteurized Milk
Learn More About Our Raw Milk
Our milk is Demeter-certified Biodynamic® and must adhere to very strict standards to maintain that certification

Hawthorne Valley Farm’s milk—both raw and pasteurized—is Demeter-certified Biodynamic® and Animal Welfare Approved, reflecting our highest commitment to purity, quality, and care for our animals. We were once one of just three farms licensed to sell raw milk in New York State. Today, as access expands, we’re proud to remain a trusted source. Our raw milk undergoes monthly inspections by the NYS Department of Agriculture and Markets and is cherished by many who find it easier to digest—and more flavorful—than conventional milk. It can only be purchased at our on-site Farm Store. Visit our FAQ page for answers to many of the questions we’ve received regarding our raw milk product.

For those seeking a safer option with many of the same benefits, our new pasteurized milk is gently heated using a low-and-slow technique that preserves much of milk’s natural goodness while eliminating risk. Whether raw or pasteurized, our milk comes from our own grass-fed herd and is handled with the same thoughtful stewardship that defines everything we do. Taste the difference of milk raised with intention, integrity, and respect.

Quark
A Versatile Dairy Delight!

Quark is a fresh, creamy dairy product that’s beloved across Europe and gaining fans around the world—and for good reason. With a texture somewhere between yogurt and soft cheese, quark is as adaptable as it is delicious.

At Hawthorne Valley, we’re proud to produce this wholesome, protein-rich food right on our Biodynamic farm. Whether you’re new to quark or a longtime fan, there are so many ways to enjoy it:

Top Ways to Enjoy Quark:
• Add a dollop to baked potatoes or soups
• Mix with herbs for a savory spread or dip
• Pair with smoked salmon, bacon, pesto, or fresh greens
• Stir in fruit and a touch of sweetener for dessert
• Spread on bread with apple butter
• Whip with cream, cocoa, and sweetener for a quick mousse

We were honored to participate in the first-ever World Quark Day in 2019, alongside the self-proclaimed Queen of Quark. Celebrated every January 19, the day highlights all that makes quark special:

A versatile ingredient for both sweet and savory dishes
A healthy alternative—low in fat, high in protein
A European staple now loved by foodies worldwide
A fun way to explore healthy, creative cooking
A chance to share recipes, tips, and discoveries

Looking for inspiration? Try one of the ideas above, or stop by our Farm Store to pick up a container and start experimenting.

Ricotta + Buttermilk

Crafted in small batches from our own certified Organic cow’s milk, our Whole Milk Ricotta and Buttermilk reflect our farm’s commitment to quality, tradition, and care for the land and animals.

Our Whole Milk Ricotta is a rich, creamy, and versatile cheese that shines in both sweet and savory dishes—from lasagna and gnocchi to pancakes and pastries. Made with whole milk from our grass-fed cows, it offers a depth of flavor and texture that reflects the vitality of the farm.

Our cultured Buttermilk is a tangy, fermented dairy drink that brings a gentle acidity and tender texture to baked goods, dressings, and marinades. Traditionally the byproduct of butter-churning, today we craft ours by fermenting our organic milk with lactic acid cultures, creating a nourishing and flavorful kitchen staple.

Essentially we’re grass farmers. We want to make sure the cows have the best diet possible.

JEREMY SHAPIRO – CREAMERY MANAGER

ABOUT THE CSA
CSA PARTNER FARMS
CSA IS THE SMARTER WAY TO BUY PRODUCE!

With a fixed cost for the year, you’ll know exactly where your food comes from: local farmers, nutrient-rich soil, and sustainable, organic and biodynamic practices that deliver high-quality, delicious produce.

Hawthorne Valley Farm has a 350–member CSA and supplies organic and Biodynamic® produce to Columbia County residents and to the New York City communities of Garden City, Inwood, and Riverdale. We also offer pick-ups at three NYC greenmarkets: 82nd Street, Union Square, and Columbia. Over 40 varieties of vegetables are grown on 16+ acres, and fruit shares from local farmers are also available. The CSA includes weekly deliveries of produce for approximately 25 weeks.

CSA SPECIFIC FAQ
View all FAQ

What is Community Supported Agriculture?

Community Supported Agriculture, or CSA, is a unique partnership between a specific farm and an individual or household. As a CSA member, you share in the risks and benefits of local, organic farming. You receive a weekly share of farm-fresh produce, get to know the life of the farm, and share in a sense of community around food, farming, nature, and nutrition. By receiving payment before the growing season begins, farmers are able to buy seeds and supplies, plan what to grow, and offset some of the risk inherent in farming, like extreme weather and crop failures. We do our best to mitigate these risks and fill any gaps that occur during the season. Through the CSA model, we commit to the close connection between farmer and eater and to growing healthy, nutritious food in a way that is environmentally and socially responsible.

What does a CSA share cost?

The cost of your CSA share varies by pick-up location and may change slightly each year. Off-farm pick-up sites are managed by dedicated CSA member volunteers, and a site fee is included in the total share price to support their efforts. For the most current pricing, please visit our sign-up page.

We understand that paying for a full share upfront can be difficult. That’s why we offer a multiple-payment option. If cost is a barrier to joining, please reach out to us via this email address to explore additional options.

What vegetables are in my CSA share through the season?

We grow over 40 types of vegetables and 120 different varieties! Read the answer to the next question below to see what a sample week would look like.

What does a typical week’s share (examples are for a full share) look like?

Each week we try to harvest a balanced variety of produce to feed two adult vegetarians, or a small family. Amount and diversity within each share changes throughout the 25 weeks (and from year to year), but here are some sample shares from this year that will give you a sense of how much of which vegetables to expect.

Week 1: 2 lettuce heads, 1/2 pound arugula, 1 bunch beets, 1 bunch swiss chard, 1 bunch scallions, 1 bunch dill

Week 5: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch kale, 1 bunch onions, 1 bunch beets, 1 bunch radishes, 2 zucchini, 1 patty-pan squash, 1 cucumber, dill, parsley

Week 10: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch swiss chard, 3 leeks, 1 bunch beets, 2 fennel bulbs, 3 pounds potatoes, 2 zucchini, 3 peppers, 5 pounds tomatoes

Week 16: 1 head lettuce, 1/2 pound arugula, 1 bunch kale, 2 delicata squash, 1 bunch salad turnips, 1 bunch broccoli rabe, 2 heads broccoli, 3 pounds potatoes, 1 bunch celeriac, 3 peppers, 2 eggplants, dill

Week 20: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch kale, 1 head bok choy, 1 green cabbage, 3 pounds potatoes, 2 leeks, 1 pie pumpkin, 3 peppers, 1 bunch turnips, 3 pounds carrots, dill

Can I split a share?

You can split a share with a friend at pick-up, or alternate weeks. Your site coordinator may be able to help pair you with another member looking to split a share.

Why does the Partial Share not get the same items as the Full Share?

We intentionally refer to it as a Partial Share rather than a “Half Share” because it doesn’t represent exactly half the quantity of a Full Share. Full Share members receive the full range and quantity of available items each week, while Partial Share members receive fewer items per week—and occasionally, different items altogether.

That said, we’ve designed the distribution so that Partial Share members receive a comparable overall balance of items over the course of the season.

What if I go on vacation?

Vacation Weeks & Share Credits
If you know in advance that you or a family member won’t be able to pick up your share, you can mark that week as a Vacation Week and receive a credit on your GrownBy account!*

To claim a Vacation Week:

Log into your GrownBy account and click “Orders” in the top right corner.

Scroll to the pick-up date you’ll be missing.

Click “Claim Vacation.”

Be sure to check all boxes for your shares and any add-ons for that week.

Your credit can be used toward future purchases in the GrownBy store. If you’re enrolled in monthly payments, it will automatically be applied to your next payment.

*Please note: Those receiving comped or donated shares are not eligible for Vacation Weeks and should arrange for a friend or family member to pick up their share during any weeks they’re unavailable.

What happens if I miss my pick up?

If you know you’ll miss your pick-up window and it’s too late to use a vacation week, your best option is to have a friend, coworker, or family member pick up your share. Just be sure they check your name off the sign-in sheet.

You’re also welcome to contact your site host to ask about possible alternatives. Many unclaimed shares are donated to local food pantries or recovery organizations.

Please note: You are not eligible for a make-up share if you miss your pick-up and do not communicate with your site host. We do not offer credits or refunds for missed shares unless they are claimed by the Sunday before (as part of your Vacation Week benefit).

Local CSA Members:
If you can’t make Thursday’s pick-up but would like to pick up over the weekend, please email Todd by Thursday at noon. Unclaimed shares are donated by Monday morning.

Are add-on’s available at every pick up site?

Some add-on items are only available at certain pick-up locations. After you select your location (step one in the purchasing platform Grownby) all of the add-on items available at that location will populate automatically. If you do not see something, that means it is not available at your chosen location.

Can I visit the farm?

Our farm is located only two hours north of NYC and we urge you to come visit us during the growing season! Members are always welcome to help out in the fields either planting, weeding, or harvesting. If you are interested in experiencing the farm this way, please contact Todd Newlin for information via email.

In addition, you may want to consider joining us for the Harvest Festival in October. This family-friendly event offers food, music, vendors, and farm-related activities. There are a couple of other festivals held on our campus that are more school-focused, but are also open to the public: the May Day Celebration and Spring Fair the first weekend of May; and the Yuletide Fair the first weekend of December. Keep an eye on the CSA newsletter for specific event details.

You are always welcome to visit the farm on your own throughout the year. If the farmers are available, we may be able to show you around. To arrange a guided tour, please complete the form at this link, and we will do our best to accommodate you. Otherwise, you can pick up a self-guided walking tour brochure at the Farm Store during business hours (7:30 a.m.-7 p.m., 7 days).

Double Up Food Bucks

Double Up Food Bucks NY (DUFBNY) doubles the buying power of SNAP customers, helping low-income families in Columbia County access healthy, locally-grown fruits and vegetables. SNAP users get up to $20 daily in extra funds to spend on fresh produce at participating markets and stores. This free program supports nutritious eating and local farmers, with funds that never expire.
Learn more

This sort of symbiotic relationship between humanism and the environment is the antidote for corporate America. We need more places like Hawthorne Valley.

OUR VALUES & STORY

At Hawthorne Valley, farming is more than a livelihood—it’s a commitment to community, sustainability, and purpose. Through hands-on education, value-added enterprises, and direct relationships with those we feed, we strive to grow in ways that nurture both the land and the human spirit.

Welcome to the Farm!
Our Approach

Welcome to Hawthorne Valley Farm—a place where farming is rooted in care, community, and connection. Since 1972, we’ve been nurturing this land in the heart of the Hudson Valley with the belief that how we grow our food matters.

Hawthorne Valley exists on the stolen ancestral land of the Mohican People, who call themselves Muh-he-con-ne-ok, or People of the Waters That Are Never Still. These lands and waters have been home to the Muh-he-con-ne-ok for countless generations. We pay respect to the Mohican People and their elders, past and present, and acknowledge the ongoing legacies of violence, displacement, and colonialism that bring us to today. We invite you to join us in uncovering the truth and pursuing a more just future.

As a certified organic and Biodynamic® farm, our approach is guided by the rhythms of nature and a deep commitment to regenerative agriculture and agroecology—ways of farming that recognize the farm as a living whole and seek to restore ecological balance. These principles echo long-standing Indigenous ways of knowing and being in relationship with the land. We strive to honor this kinship by tending soil, plants, animals, and community in a spirit of reciprocity, respect, and care.

We invite you to learn more about the values that shape our work, the story behind our fields and forests, and the people who bring this vibrant farm to life each day.

OUR MISSION AND VISION

Nurturing the Land That Nurtures Us

At Hawthorne Valley Farm, we’ve been committed to biodynamic and organic agriculture since 1972. As a diversified, 900-acre Biodynamic® farm in upstate New York, our mission is to care for the land, grow food that nourishes, and foster a deep connection between people and the source of their sustenance.

Biodynamic agriculture is a holistic, ecological practice that works with natural systems, not against them. We never use GMOs, synthetic chemicals, or pesticides. Instead, we build fertility through composting, rotational grazing, and crop diversity—practices that build healthy soil and create a self-sustaining farm organism.

Our approach integrates plants, animals, and people into a living, breathing whole. From our dairy herd and grain fields to our vegetable gardens and forested pastures, everything plays a role in sustaining the balance of the farm and its community.

Our History

Rooted in Purpose: The Farm’s Founding Vision (1972-1993)

Hawthorne Valley Farm was established in 1972 to serve as the foundation for what is now known as the Visiting Students Program—an immersive farm-based educational experience. From the beginning, the mission was twofold: to be a working biodynamic farm and a place of learning. This “dual mandate” was essential to ensure both educational value and financial sustainability. Of note, in 1985, Hawthorne Valley Farm became one of the first farms in the United States to obtain Biodynamic certification from the newly established Demeter US. As the farm grew, it expanded into several departments—including a dairy, bakery, farm store, and presence at NYC’s Union Square Greenmarket—yet by 1993, financial challenges put its future in jeopardy.

 

A Turning Point: Renewal and Resilience (1993-1998)

With the farm facing deep financial crisis, a leadership transition in 1994 brought in Steffen and Rachel Schneider to rebuild. Through the creation of new management structures, the founding of the CSA, and a renewed focus on biodynamic practices, the farm slowly found its footing. Each department began to stabilize, and the CSA expanded from 30 to over 250 members. That same year, Hawthorne Valley co-founded the Collaborative Regional Alliance for Farmer Training (C.R.A.F.T.), a network of local organic and biodynamic farms dedicated to enhancing educational experiences for farm apprentices. The Annual Fall Festival was launched in 1995, and by 1998, the farm had turned a profit, developed its first Five-Year Plan, and emerged with a renewed sense of purpose.

 

Growing Together: Stability and Cultural Recognition (1998-2009)

This period marked a maturation of Hawthorne Valley Farm’s identity. A dedicated team carried the mission forward with passion and resilience. As food systems and sustainable agriculture entered mainstream conversations, the farm gained recognition through media coverage, speaking engagements, and consultancy requests. In 2000, the creation of a campus-wide Master Plan catalyzed future development, including the construction of the new Farm Store (2003–2004). The farm also deepened its educational role by welcoming the Farmscape Ecology Program, expanding staff, and refining leadership roles to support its growing complexity and impact.

 

A Decade of Growth, Innovation, and Community Impact (2010–2021)

Beginning in 2010 with a $2.5 million grant for farmstead improvements, Hawthorne Valley Farm has continued to evolve and grow while staying true to its mission. The farm earned Animal Welfare Approved certification in 2011 and significantly expanded in 2015 with the acquisition of Twin Maple Farm and 50 additional acres on Schnackenberg Road, reuniting parts of the historic Burfeind Farm. That same year, a USDA grant launched the Farm Beginnings program for aspiring farmers. In 2016, our Creamery introduced its signature watercolor cow label, and in 2017, we kicked off the Healthy Food for All Initiative, leading to the launch of Rolling Grocer 19’s mobile market in 2018 and a storefront in Hudson by 2019. Also in 2019, there was a transition in Farm leadership and Spencer Fenniman become the Director of Farming. A Place Corps silvopasture project took root in 2020, and 2021 brought new infrastructure, including a biodynamic prep station and CSA cold storage. Rolling Grocer 19 became fully community-led that year, reflecting our ongoing commitment to food access and community resilience.

 

Three Years of Growth: Building Soil, Community, and Climate Resilience (2022-2024)

From 2022 to 2024, Hawthorne Valley Farm deepened its commitment to education, collaboration, and ecological stewardship. It hosted The Climate Farm School, joined the Hudson Valley Bulk Order program, and partnered with local farmer-led software startup GrownBy to streamline CSA operations. A capital campaign funded new deer fencing, while research with Yale explored basalt’s role in soil carbon capture. The farm became Real Organic Project Certified and promoted regenerative practices regionally. Educational offerings expanded for students from Hawthorne Valley, Bard, and Williams College. Enrolled in NRCS’s Conservation Stewardship Program, the farm saw major gains in soil health and efficiency through cover cropping, fallowing, and high tunnel use. In 2024, CRAFT celebrated its 30th anniversary.

Interested in digging deeper into our history? Click this link to read our 50th Anniversary Commemorative.

How We Are Unconventional By Nature

Our farm embodies Hawthorne Valley’s tagline—unconventional by nature—by challenging the norms of modern industrial agriculture and embracing a holistic, regenerative approach to land and community. We leave horns on our cows, raise animals with dignity, and prioritize biodiversity over efficiency. Rather than scaling up through monocultures or automation, we grow through relationships—adding value to our raw ingredients through our creamery, bakery, and farm store, and connecting directly with the people we feed. Every choice we make reflects a deep respect for the natural world and a belief that farming can nourish both ecological and human health. In this way, our farm is not just a place of production, but a living expression of values that run counter to convention—and deeply in tune with nature.

How The Land We Steward Feeds Our Community

At Hawthorne Valley, the land we steward nourishes more than bodies—it nurtures connections, learning, and a sense of shared purpose. As a true Biodynamic farm, our goal is to cultivate food of the highest quality while caring deeply for the health of our soil, animals, and ecosystem. Every harvest reflects our commitment to sustainability, balance, and reverence for the natural world.

Through our farm store, bakery, and creamery, we add value to what we grow and raise, allowing us to farm at a human scale without placing undue stress on the land. By selling directly to our community—on the farm, at Greenmarkets in NYC, and through our CSA—we create opportunities for meaningful relationships between people and the source of their food.

This nourishment extends beyond the plate. Children, students, and young adults engage with the farm through educational visits, vocational training, and seasonal work, deepening their understanding of where food comes from and how farming practices shape our environment and our lives. These experiences help cultivate not just future farmers, but thoughtful stewards of the earth.

In this way, the land feeds our bodies and our community—it teaches, connects, and inspires.

Why We Believe in Direct-to-Consumer

We believe in direct-to-consumer marketing because it allows us to grow our farm in a balanced, intentional way—reducing stress on the land, plants, and animals while staying true to a human scale of farming. By adding value to our raw ingredients through our creamery, farm store, and bakery, and selling those products directly through our farm store, CSA program, and Greenmarkets in NYC, we’re able to avoid the industrial, monoculture-based farming models that dominate much of agriculture today. These direct channels not only offer greater financial sustainability through higher profit margins, but also foster lasting social connections—bringing people onto the farm, deepening their understanding of where their food comes from, and nurturing a shared sense of purpose. Supplying food to Hawthorne Valley’s school, summer camp, and visiting student programs further strengthens these relationships and reinforces our commitment to community-centered farming.

Education, Apprenticeships & Youth Programs

Our farm serves as a vibrant educational hub where learning is rooted in the rhythms of the land. Through hands-on experiences in farming, food production, and land stewardship, we welcome students, apprentices, and visitors of all ages to engage with the complexities and rewards of sustainable agriculture. Whether through our school, summer camp, visiting student programs, or vocational training, we offer immersive opportunities to explore what it means to live in harmony with nature and contribute to a more just and resilient food system. This integration of education and agriculture allows us to cultivate not just crops, but a deeper understanding of our interconnectedness with the earth and each other.

FAQS
FAQS

Have questions? You’re not alone. We’ve gathered answers to some of the most common questions about our farm, practices, products, and more.

If you can’t find the answers to your questions here, please don’t hesitate to reach out.

GENERAL

What is Biodynamics?

Biodynamics: Farming in Harmony with Nature

Biodynamics is often described as “organic plus.” Like organic farming, it avoids synthetic chemicals, but it goes further—viewing the farm as a self-sustaining, living organism. Plants, animals, and people all play essential roles in a balanced, interconnected system. For example, composted manure from our animals nourishes the soil that grows our vegetables, creating a closed-loop of fertility.

We also use specially prepared natural remedies—called Biodynamic preparations—on our fields and compost piles to enhance soil vitality. These preparations, along with attention to lunar and planetary rhythms, help support the health and resilience of our farm.

Developed in the early 20th century, Biodynamics emerged before chemical agriculture took hold. It was introduced by Austrian philosopher Rudolf Steiner, who also inspired Waldorf education and the spiritual science of Anthroposophy. In 1924, Steiner delivered a series of lectures outlining a holistic approach to farming—one that works in partnership with the life forces of nature to regenerate the land and nourish both body and spirit.

Learn more

Are you certified organic?

Yes. Our farm is certified organic according to the federal government’s USDA organic standards. We are also Real Organic Project certified, which is an add-on to the USDA Organic certification. Why, you may ask, is this necessary?

While the USDA Organic label once stood for a deep commitment to soil health, animal welfare, and ecological balance, enforcement of those standards has weakened over time. Industrial operations can now earn the same seal without truly following organic principles—making it harder for farms like ours to stand out.

That’s why we’ve chosen to be certified by the Real Organic Project, an “add-on” label created by farmers to uphold the original spirit of organic farming. Real Organic certification ensures transparency and integrity by requiring practices like growing in healthy soil (not hydroponically) and raising animals on pasture.

By supporting farms with the Real Organic label, you’re helping protect the future of truly regenerative, soil-based agriculture.

What is Demeter?

Demeter is the certifying agency for Biodynamic farms. It is an international organization with affiliates in many other countries.

When you see the Demeter Certified Biodynamic® label, it means the farm or product meets strict standards for holistic, regenerative farming. Demeter, the nonprofit that holds the Biodynamic trademark, ensures that every certified farm nurtures soil health, biodiversity, and the integrity of the entire ecosystem.

Just like with “organic,” clear standards matter. That’s why Demeter certification is renewed annually—to protect the meaning behind Biodynamic and give you confidence in what you’re supporting.

Where is your farm? Can I visit?

Our farm is in Columbia County, New York, near the city of Hudson, about 2 1/2 hours’ drive north of New York City. Visitors are welcome. Guided tours are available if planned in advance by either calling our Marketing Director (518-672-4465 x 222), or filling out a tour request form; visitors are also welcome to take self-guided tours using the maps available in our Farm Store.

Are you connected to a school?

Our farm is part of the same non-profit association as Hawthorne Valley  Waldorf School, an early childhood through grade 12 independent school that is nestled within our campus, across the street from our farm store and milking barn. Students from the school visit and work on the farm as part of their curriculum.

Are your cows free range/pastured?

Yes. They are only in the barn when necessary during the grazing season — during our twice-a-day milking sessions. In winter when the pastures are fallow, the cows share a large, airy loafing shed and yard, and are brought into the milking barn twice a day. There may also be times throughout the year when the weather is too extreme for them to be out.

What do you feed your cows?

From spring through fall, they rotationally graze our pastures, helping to build soil health and fertility. In the colder months, they’re nourished with homegrown Biodynamic® hay and fermented baleage we harvest and store during the summer, along with salt, minerals, and kelp for balanced nutrition. Our cows are never given hormones or antibiotics.

How many cows do you have?

Our herd size fluctuates but, generally, we have about 65 dairy cows. We also raise a small herd of steers for beef.

What do your pigs eat?

A variety of organic foods including the whey that is produced when we make our yogurt, unclaimed leftover bakery products, organic produce and other leftovers from our store’s deli, stems and seconds from the vegetable fields, and plants and insects that they scavenge for themselves while rooting around in their pastures. If these sources run short, we supplement with organic grain.

PRODUCTS

Is your milk A2?

No. In order for milk to be considered A2, each cow in the herd must be tested for this genetic marker. While the Brown Swiss breed has a higher rate of this gene, and this breed is dominant among our herd, there are many other breeds mixed in.

What is raw milk?

Simply put, raw milk is milk that has not been pasteurized or homogenized.

Is raw milk nutritionally different from conventional pasteurized milk?

Raw milk is minimally processed, and considered a ‘live food product’ – it hasn’t been pasteurized, or heated. As a result its enzymes are fully active, and it contains beneficial bacteria, 22 amino acids, OMEGA-3 fatty acids, vitamins, immunoglobulins, minerals, antioxidants, and natural CLA.

Is raw milk safe to drink?

Raw milk that produced under sanitary conditions is a safe and healthy food. It is important that the cows are healthy (tested free of TB and undulant fever) and do not have any infections (such as mastitis). The cows should be eating food appropriate to cows, which is mostly grass, hay or silage, with only a small amount of grain, if any. The milk should be full-fat milk, as many important anti-microbial and health-supporting components are in the fat. The cows must be milked under sanitary conditions and the milk chilled down immediately. (source: Campaign for Real Milk, an initiative of the Weston A. Price Foundation) Read the answer to our next question to learn about our sanitation practices.

How do you ensure the safety of your raw milk?

Our commitment to quality and safety starts with rigorous certification and inspection processes. All dairies in New York State, including ours, are certified by the U.S. Department of Agriculture and Markets approximately every five years, and undergo monthly inspections by New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.

To ensure the utmost sanitation and safety of our milk, we’ve implemented a strict process that includes:

Bulk Tank Cleaning: We meticulously clean our bulk tank before refilling it with fresh milk, ensuring the freshest product possible. This process is monitored by a chart recorder attached to the bulk tank, which constantly tracks temperature and time. The inspector reviews these charts monthly, confirming that the milk is consistently stored below 38 degrees Fahrenheit.
Antibiotic Testing: Despite being a certified Organic and Biodynamic farm that prohibits antibiotic use, we are still required by the state of New York to test each batch of milk for antibiotics. This is crucial as even some certified organic farms have been found with antibiotics present. Our commitment to purity is unwavering.
Bacteria Testing: We voluntarily conduct a 24-hour bacteria test for E.coli, Salmonella, and other harmful bacteria. While many small farms lack the capability for such thorough testing, we prioritize this step to ensure our milk’s safety. If any high bacteria count is detected (though it never has been), we would refrain from sending that milk to the store. Given that we sell a significant volume of raw milk—between 60-120 gallons per week—this extra precaution is essential.

At Hawthorne Valley Farm, the safety and quality of our raw milk are paramount. Our rigorous processes ensure you receive the best-tasting, safest milk possible.

Where can I buy your raw milk?

According to New York State law, raw milk can only be sold on the farm. You can buy it at our on-site Farm Store.

Do you sell pasteurized milk?

We do! This spring, our creamery introduced Biodynamic® and organic pasteurized milk to its product line. Pasteurized milk in quart and half gallon sizes are now available at the Farm Store and our market stands in New York City.

You can find our pasteurized Biodynamic, organic milk in quart and half gallon sizes at these locations:

Farm Store
Union Square – Broadway near 17th Street (Wednesdays & Saturdays)
Inwood – Isham Street between cooper & Seaman Avenues (Saturdays)
Columbia University – East side of Broadway between 114th and 115th Streets (Sundays)
82nd Street, St. Stephen’s Greenmarket, Manhattan (Saturdays)
Jackson Heights Greenmarket, Queens (Sundays)
Dag Hammarskjold – East 47th St &, 2nd Ave (Wednesdays)
Brooklyn Borough Hall – On plaza at Court St and Montague St (Saturdays)
CREATING A SUSTAINABLE SYSTEM

Hawthorne Valley Farm’s Creamery is proud to contribute to a sustainable regional milk supply chain by offering co-packing services for small local farms. The additional capacity to process pasteurized fluid milk will provide additional opportunities for the local dairy industry.

CSA

What is Community Supported Agriculture?

Community Supported Agriculture, or CSA, is a unique partnership between a specific farm and an individual or household. As a CSA member, you share in the risks and benefits of local, organic farming. You receive a weekly share of farm-fresh produce, get to know the life of the farm, and share in a sense of community around food, farming, nature, and nutrition. By receiving payment before the growing season begins, farmers are able to buy seeds and supplies, plan what to grow, and offset some of the risk inherent in farming, like extreme weather and crop failures. We do our best to mitigate these risks and fill any gaps that occur during the season. Through the CSA model, we commit to the close connection between farmer and eater and to growing healthy, nutritious food in a way that is environmentally and socially responsible.

What does a CSA share cost?

The cost of your CSA share varies by pick-up location and may change slightly each year. Off-farm pick-up sites are managed by dedicated CSA member volunteers, and a site fee is included in the total share price to support their efforts. For the most current pricing, please visit our sign-up page.

We understand that paying for a full share upfront can be difficult. That’s why we offer a multiple-payment option. If cost is a barrier to joining, please reach out via this email, to explore additional options.

What vegetables are in my CSA share through the season?

We grow over 40 types of vegetables and 120 different varieties! Read the answer to the next question below to see what a sample week would look like.

What does a typical week’s share (examples are for a full share) look like?

Each week we try to harvest a balanced variety of produce to feed two adult vegetarians, or a small family. Amount and diversity within each share changes throughout the 25 weeks (and from year to year), but here are some sample shares from this year that will give you a sense of how much of which vegetables to expect.

Week 1: 2 lettuce heads, 1/2 pound arugula, 1 bunch beets, 1 bunch swiss chard, 1 bunch scallions, 1 bunch dill

Week 5: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch kale, 1 bunch onions, 1 bunch beets, 1 bunch radishes, 2 zucchini, 1 patty-pan squash, 1 cucumber, dill, parsley

Week 10: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch swiss chard, 3 leeks, 1 bunch beets, 2 fennel bulbs, 3 pounds potatoes, 2 zucchini, 3 peppers, 5 pounds tomatoes

Week 16: 1 head lettuce, 1/2 pound arugula, 1 bunch kale, 2 delicata squash, 1 bunch salad turnips, 1 bunch broccoli rabe, 2 heads broccoli, 3 pounds potatoes, 1 bunch celeriac, 3 peppers, 2 eggplants, dill

Week 20: 1 head lettuce, 1 bunch kale, 1 head bok choy, 1 green cabbage, 3 pounds potatoes, 2 leeks, 1 pie pumpkin, 3 peppers, 1 bunch turnips, 3 pounds carrots, dill

Can I split a share?

You can split a share with a friend at pick-up, or alternate weeks. Your site coordinator may be able to help pair you with another member looking to split a share.

Why does the Partial Share not get the same items as the Full Share?

We intentionally refer to it as a Partial Share rather than a “Half Share” because it doesn’t represent exactly half the quantity of a Full Share. Full Share members receive the full range and quantity of available items each week, while Partial Share members receive fewer items per week—and occasionally, different items altogether.

That said, we’ve designed the distribution so that Partial Share members receive a comparable overall balance of items over the course of the season.

What if I go on vacation?

Vacation Weeks & Share Credits
If you know in advance that you or a family member won’t be able to pick up your share, you can mark that week as a Vacation Week and receive a credit on your GrownBy account!*

To claim a Vacation Week:

Log into your GrownBy account and click “Orders” in the top right corner.

Scroll to the pick-up date you’ll be missing.

Click “Claim Vacation.”

Be sure to check all boxes for your shares and any add-ons for that week.

Your credit can be used toward future purchases in the GrownBy store. If you’re enrolled in monthly payments, it will automatically be applied to your next payment.

*Please note: Those receiving comped or donated shares are not eligible for Vacation Weeks and should arrange for a friend or family member to pick up their share during any weeks they’re unavailable.

What happens if I miss my pick up?

If you know you’ll miss your pick-up window and it’s too late to use a vacation week, your best option is to have a friend, coworker, or family member pick up your share. Just be sure they check your name off the sign-in sheet.

You’re also welcome to contact your site host to ask about possible alternatives. Many unclaimed shares are donated to local food pantries or recovery organizations.

Please note: You are not eligible for a make-up share if you miss your pick-up and do not communicate with your site host. We do not offer credits or refunds for missed shares unless they are claimed by the Sunday before (as part of your Vacation Week benefit).

Local CSA Members:
If you can’t make Thursday’s pick-up but would like to pick up over the weekend, please email Betsy by Thursday at noon. Unclaimed shares are donated by Monday morning.

Are add-on’s available at every pick up site?

Some add-on items are only available at certain pick-up locations. After you select your location (step one in the purchasing platform Grownby) all of the add-on items available at that location will populate automatically. If you do not see something, that means it is not available at your chosen location.

WHERE TO BUY

Whether you’re visiting our campus in the Hudson Valley, our greenmarket stands in NYC, or shopping at a regional natural foods store, there are many ways to bring our fresh, organic products into your kitchen.

BRINGING THE FARM TO YOU

Our products are available year-round at our Farm Store, through our CSA program, at select NYC Greenmarkets, and at a growing number of regional natural food stores. Choose what works best for you and enjoy food that’s thoughtfully grown and full of life.

NYC Greenmarkets
See Our NYC Greenmarkets Schedule

Since 1980, we’ve been bringing the bounty of our farm to New York City’s Union Square Greenmarket, expanding to Inwood in 2004 and now also attending the Columbia Market, Dag Hammarskjold Plaza Greenmarket, Jackson Heights Market, St. Stephen’s (82nd St.), and Borough Hall in Brooklyn. These weekly visits are more than just market days—they’re opportunities to connect city dwellers with the rhythms of rural life and the nourishment of fresh, local, Biodynamic® and organic food.

Our stands are filled with farm-grown and farm-crafted offerings, including pasteurized milk, yogurts, cheeses, sauerkrauts, kim chee, breads, and baked goods. When ingredients can’t be grown on-site, we source them as locally and responsibly as possible. We also bring a rotating selection of fresh produce, harvested in season and grown with the utmost care. All of our products are USDA Organic and Real Organic Project certified, and our vegetables carry the additional distinction of being Demeter-certified Biodynamic.

Farm Store
Learn more

You can find all of Hawthorne Valley Farm’s certified Organic and Biodynamic products right here at our Farm Store. We offer raw and pasteurized milk from our grass-fed dairy herd, along with a variety of certified organic cultured dairy products crafted in our creamery, including yogurt (Plain, Maple, Honey, and Coffee), buttermilk, ricotta, and quark. Our plain yogurt is also certified Biodynamic, as is our milk which also carries the Animal Welfare Approved certification.

We proudly raise cows, pigs, and chickens on pasture, and their meats are available seasonally in the store. Our beef is certified organic, Biodynamic, and Animal Welfare Approved, with cuts ranging from steaks and ground beef to bones and organs. Our whey-fed pork is raised to organic standards and typically includes chops, sausages, ground pork, and sugar-free smoked bacon. During the growing season, we also offer certified organic, pasture-raised chicken, available whole or halved, with parts like necks, livers, and feet available by request.

Our Demeter-certified Biodynamic farm also grows over 40 varieties of vegetables on 16+ acres, and you’ll find these fresh, delicious, and nutrient-rich veggies seasonally in our store’s produce department. Availability may vary, but the care and quality behind every product remain constant.

Find Us Beyond the Farm

In addition to our own Farm Store, you can find our products at a growing number of regional natural food stores. We’re proud to partner with like-minded retailers who share our commitment to quality, sustainability, and nourishing communities.

If your local grocer doesn’t yet carry our products, we’d be grateful if you asked them to consider doing so. Your voice makes a real difference and helps small farms like ours thrive. Thank you for supporting regenerative agriculture and choosing to eat with intention.

ABOUT THE CSA
CSA PARTNER FARMS
CSA PARTNER FARMS

Our CSA is made possible through collaboration with a community of like-minded farms who share our commitment to organic and regenerative agriculture. Together, we’re able to offer an abundant, seasonal variety while supporting a resilient regional food system.

Farm at Miller’s Crossing
Learn more

The Farm at Miller’s Crossing is a certified organic, family-run farm in Hudson, NY. Spanning 200 scenic acres along the Agawamuck Creek, the farm is stewarded by Chris and Katie Cashen and their extended family. With a focus on ecological health, right livelihood, and seasonal abundance, they grow a wide variety of vegetables, flowers, and grass-fed beef. We’re proud to partner with them through our CSA to bring their fresh, local harvests to our community.

Kinderhook Creek Farm

Kinderhook Creek Farm, located in Stephentown, NY, is a third-generation family farm run by the Eckhardts. For over 60 years, they’ve been known for their farm-fresh sweet corn, high-quality hay and grain, and vibrant seasonal produce. Farming over 1,200 acres in Rensselaer County, they cultivate a strong connection to the land and their community. We’re honored to partner with them through our CSA to share their abundant, locally grown harvests.

MX Morningstar Farm
Learn more

MX Morningstar Farm is a diversified vegetable farm located on 30 acres in the heart of Claverack, NY. Since 2014, they’ve been dedicated to growing high-quality produce using sustainable practices that nurture the land and community. Their holistic approach enhances both flavor and soil health, resulting in abundant, nutrient-rich harvests. We’re proud to partner with them through our CSA to offer their fresh, responsibly grown vegetables to our members each season.

FISHKILL FARMS
Learn more

Fishkill Farms is a 270-acre family-run orchard and vegetable farm in East Fishkill, NY, proudly stewarded by the Morgenthau family for over a century. They grow organic vegetables and eco-certified fruit, offering fresh, seasonal bounty through their CSA, farm store, pick-your-own events, and regional farmers markets. From spring strawberries to fall apples, Fishkill Farms blends sustainable farming with community-centered experiences—and we’re proud to bring their harvests to our CSA members.

MEAD ORCHARDS FARM
Learn more

Mead Orchards, located in Tivoli, NY, is a fourth-generation family farm with over a century of fruit-growing heritage. Since 1916, the Mead family has expanded from apples to a vibrant array of fruits and vegetables—all grown with care and innovation. Today, Chuck Mead continues the legacy, offering pick-your-own experiences and selling at local farmers markets. We’re proud to partner with Mead Orchards to bring their delicious, seasonal produce to our CSA members.

GRINDSTONE FARM
Learn more

Grindstone Farm has been a pioneer in organic farming for over 40 years, growing high-quality, NOFA-certified organic fruits and vegetables in northern New York. Based in Pulaski, they not only cultivate their own produce but also collaborate with other organic farms to offer a wide range of sustainably raised goods. We’re proud to partner with Grindstone Farm to bring their nutrient-rich, responsibly grown offerings to our CSA members each season.
